chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated from Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abdurrahman ibn Katheer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah: 'Has come the command of Allah, so do not hasten it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate [with Him].'

He said: It is our matter (the appearance of the Qa'im). Allah commanded that you do not hasten it until Allah supports it with three armies: the angels, the believers, and terror. His advent is like the advent of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And that is His saying, Exalted is He: 'As your Lord caused you to go forth from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were surely averse.'

key_terms.أَمْرُنَا: Our matter (referring to the appearance of the Qa'im)

ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'Atha amrullah' refer to in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Al-Nu'mani records Abu Abdillah’s (as) interpretation of 'Atha amrullah' as a direct reference to the Qa'im’s appearance, emphasizing that divine timing requires patience until Allah supports the cause with three armies: angels, believers, and terror. This emergence is likened to the Prophet’s migration (Hijra), invoking the verse where Allah brought him forth with truth despite the reluctance of some believers, highlighting the continuity of divine authority and the inevitability of the Imam's rise.
